rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Walk-away test (M2+).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L45: 'The checks pay twice: a session they steer is a session you don't babysit, and a session you don't babysit can run beside another.' Closest to violating only in that it argues FOR the walk-away rather than staging it; the staging is real and load-bearing elsewhere — L70 'The packaged session returns after this sitting ends' puts the packaged re-send outside the sitting entirely, which is the maximum trust distance the arc has reached. No read-every-reply-and-paste-back beat anywhere in the body (the one prompt at L33 is a single question, not a turn loop).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design — no human backstops.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L73 is the line closest to a backstop: 'The verifier's green is a claim, not proof. Ask the agent to show what the gate checked and what sat outside its view before you credit the kit.' It stays inside because the audit is routed to the AGENT (ask it to show), not to a human re-derivation, and the student's role is the trust-line decision ('before you credit the kit') — exactly the irreversible/trust-line exception the rule preserves. No 'Antti observes' or if-then ruleset on an agent flow anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One exercise = one bounded activity.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module includes exactly two exercise files, L49 [Exercise: Fork the worktree, carry the evidence] and L51 [Exercise: Diagnose and re-send], each a separate bounded activity (fork/setup vs diagnose→build→assemble→re-send). No sub-numbering in the module body: grep -nE 'Exercise [0-9]|Part [0-9][ab]' on the body returned 0. The internal do→observe→adjust arc of diagnose-and-resend stays one exercise, which is what the rule asks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Modules composable across variants.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The file forks nothing; it uses in-file VARIANT markers exactly as prescribed — L67 '<!--flag:no-module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop-->' / L89 closing it, and L101 '<!--flag:module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop-->' / L120 closing it, so the no-M6 close (L68-87) and the M6 bridge (L102-118) live in ONE file. Body is includes + framing: five bare-path include links (L37, L47, L49, L51, L55, L57), no copied exercise or lecture prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Three-level completeness.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three levels present and chain backwards cleanly: strategy frame at L3-4 (Big Idea) and L13-19 (Bloom LOs); runtime artifact a trainer reads at a blocker at L177-185 (Push-back moves), L193-198 (Decision points — pacing) and L223-234 (per-phase failure/escape table); sendable student asset is the body L21-118, which produces the input M6 consumes (L104, 'A packaged session with substance'). Closest to a gap is the trainer layer's dependence on the linked exercise for phase names, but the phase labels are quoted verbatim in the table's first column so the lookup resolves without opening the exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pattern-recognition LOs need n≥2 instances with contrast.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L15 is the pattern-recognition LO: '**Diagnose** your un-packaged send-off through three named lenses… grounded in quoted moments from the return'. n≥2 with contrast is satisfied by design and named in the body: read #1 is the M4 un-packaged return (L23, 'You walk in with the artefact in front of you'), read #2 is the packaged return (L70-72, 'Give it the read the first return got: the three lenses… Where the two sessions disagree is the local evidence'). The gap between the two reads IS the module's variable (packaging), which is exactly the contrast condition the rule requires.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Progression-with-variations is the spine.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The send-off move is on its second face, not repeated verbatim: M4 sends un-packaged, M5 sends the SAME task packaged and reads the contrast (L19 '**Re-send** the packaged version of the same task'; L74 'the loop you just ran is yours to keep running'). The figure re-show at L79 '{{figure:map-engine-m4-open}}' is the load-bearing model the rule's carve-out licenses: it is priced as dosage/placement (L76 heading '## Back to the map, one last time'), and the placement is self-sufficient — L81-83 re-states the dashed edge and defines 'the wall' rather than assuming the earlier reading.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student agency — adults decide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L106 is the closest to compulsion: 'Come to Module 6 without the packaged session and you'll have one session to read where the exercise needs two. Your call.' It stays inside because it prices the consequence and hands the decision back in the same breath — the rule's ship-step carve-out (artifact feeding the next phase) would even license a harder ask. Elsewhere agency is explicit: L91-94 'Optional challenges… Pick one when you want', L109-111 'Optional', L11 'Optional prep', L35 'if you want to live with it a week'. No forced-pacing phrasing (grep for 'sit for|don't scan|take N minutes' returned 0 on the body).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Delegation — student brings, Claude screens.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body's single delegated ask is L33 {{prompt:ae101-m5-done-done}}, whose body is 'Are we done-done? By done-done I mean: 1) tests… 4) security… Answer per point, with evidence from this session.' Access: the session's own transcript, which Claude holds by construction — no Jira/Linear/wiki surface is named anywhere in the body. Judgement: the student brings the session and the criteria are supplied; Claude fit-screens against named criteria, which the rule assigns to the agent. The student keeps the choices the rule reserves for them — which failure is dominant (L74), whether the definition lands in a file and where (L35).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Split mega-exercise when phases = distinct skills + distinct artifacts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Already split, and split on the rule's own axis: L49 fork-the-worktree (skill: fork from the M4 SHA; artifact: the worktree branch, contract row at L214) and L51 diagnose-and-resend (skills: diagnose/build/assemble/re-send; artifacts: reference, plan.md, verifier, RUN-NOTES.md, contract rows L215-218). Narrative survives by artifact chaining — the worktree row's 'Consumed by' column names 'M5 packaged re-send (runs in worktree)'. The maintainer note at L128 records the most recent split ('## Set up the worktree moved into exercises/fork-the-worktree.md as Phase 1 bullets').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-realism check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every named path in the body exists or is created by an earlier beat: './CLAUDE.md' and './CLAUDE.local.md' (L35, L83) are Claude Code runtime files, no install; '../<repo>-m5' worktree is created by the exercise at L49 before any beat depends on it; '~/.claude/projects/<project>/' appears only in the maintainer block (L178). The one prompt (L33) names no tool, skill, connector or file to install — it asks a question of the live session. No (a)/(b)/(c) 'no' anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique — default.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L29 carries the WHY: 'A done-done definition is a small context trick that buys repeated fast verification: every run, and every check you build, measures against the same line.' L35 carries the HOW and where: 'putting the definition in ./CLAUDE.md once… ./CLAUDE.local.md first if you want to live with it a week.' The closest black-box risk is L17's menu of shapes ('LLM judge, shell-hook, or Ralph re-feed') in the LO list, but nothing in the module body asks the student to USE them unexplained — the deconstruction is scheduled and named (L55 what-packaging-is, L57 the-gate-is-a-claim), which is orientation, not invocation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Auto-fire sim+eval after significant rewrite.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule, observable on this file only through its evaluation record, which is present and current-shaped: L162 '**Quality:** sim-passed 2026-08-29 (writing@4a722813 story@441b361f technical@8cc00874 behavior@b55cd28b pedagogy@441b361f strategy@17446703 slides@17446703)', L163 the per-class judge row, L164 the cross_module row at module-set scope. Seven per-class SHAs plus both scope rows are recorded, i.e. the sim+eval fired rather than being deferred. I did not run the staleness scanner, so whether each pin is current against HEAD is unverified here and belongs to the orchestrator's stamp check, not to this rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module's one forcing function is fenced: L33 {{prompt:ae101-m5-done-done}}. The one prose exception is '## Inspect your results' (L68-74), which carries its own dated accept-note at L126: '`## Inspect your results` stays prose, no fence (accepted 2026-08-20)… it fires after the sitting ends, on a return whose artefact paths do not exist at authoring time, so a fence would have to invent them… Do not add a fence, and do not cut it.' L104 ('Read the scrollback or commits from the re-send') is Boundary-2 light-homework register, not session machinery. No scripted reactions: the body's counts are 'once' (L35, a design principle) and 'pay twice' (L45, a metaphor) — no bare imperative count anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Personal-first, team promotion via human conversation.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L83-85 is the rule stated as body prose, correctly: 'A rule in your own ./CLAUDE.local.md sits on your side of it. The same rule in a repo's ./CLAUDE.md, loading into a teammate's session whether they asked for it or not, has crossed… prove it on yourself, then promote.' L87 routes promotion through the human channel: 'the first move across is one rule, proven on you, promoted through your team's normal PR.' L35 applies the same order to the done-done definition (CLAUDE.local.md first, CLAUDE.md is 'a PR-sized change').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification layers sample DIFFERENT error distributions — not belt-and-braces.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L72-73 keeps the layers distinct rather than stacking them: 'Where the two sessions disagree is the local evidence: which failure the kit caught, and which still recurs' (contrast layer) and 'The verifier's green is a claim, not proof. Ask the agent to show what the gate checked and what sat outside its view' (blind-spot layer). L43 adds a third distribution — the remembered mid-run worry tested against the artefact. Each names a different error shape, and L74 refuses to declare done on one clean pass: 'What recurs names your next check.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cheap-before-expensive verification ordering.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L73 is the closest call: the cheap tier (ask the agent what the gate checked) is required BEFORE the expensive tier (crediting the kit and building on it) — 'before you credit the kit' is the ordering word. L43's worry-test against the return is likewise cheap-first, and the expensive tier (build a verifier, re-send) comes after at L45. Nothing in the body spends an expensive layer on something that failed a cheap one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cohort execution is trainer-paced + concurrent, not sequential.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L167 (maintainer Pacing): 'Runtime is computed — node scripts/calculate-time.js learn-from-the-test. Trainer demos slowly, room copy-pastes concurrently.' Concurrency is also priced explicitly rather than summed at L169: 'Fork is a band because the spread is real. Machine time is ~1 min… the rest is coordinates-read, copy-verification and Day-2 re-entry fumble.' The long agent wait is treated as elapsed-outside-the-sitting, not as summed student time (L70, 'The packaged session returns after this sitting ends').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Host-skill optional; maintainer blocks trainer-only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c 'Nerd' on the file → 0. Header is exactly the prescribed form at L177: '**Push-back moves** (trainer delivers)'. Every bullet and every Escape-hatch cell names the trainer as actor ('Trainer push:', L179-184; 'Trainer surfaces the menu again', L182; 'Trainer: don't.', L234). No 'Trainer / Nerd push:' and no '(trainer in cohort; Nerd in self-study)' parenthetical anywhere. No host-skill is named as prework or prereq — L6-11 Prework asks only for the M4 session plus optional reading.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats: in-chat over file-write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module body asks for no reflective file write at all — grep -nEi 'write (a|your) .*\.md|create a file|save (it|this)' on the body projection returned 0 hits. The one reflective beat (L33's done-done prompt) is in-chat by explicit design, and the maintainer note at L124 gives the downstream-reader reason the rule asks for: 'the student pastes ae101-m5-done-done into that session, so the per-point audit lands in the transcript diagnose-and-resend reads… Question form rather than a file write for that reason.' The file writes that do exist (reference, plan.md, RUN-NOTES.md) all have named downstream readers in the artefact-contract table at L215-218.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi '\b(room|group|pair|discuss|share|together|neighbour|classmate|partner|everyone)\b' on the body projection returns exactly ONE hit, L16, and it is the LO verb '**Pair** each failure mode with the packaging that catches it' — a matching operation on failure modes, not a human pairing. No trainer-cue beat, no pause-cue, no 'discuss with' sentence. Every body sentence is about work (artifact, prompt, next action); cohort management lives entirely in the maintainer block (L167 pacing, L177-185 pushes), which is not a runtime script.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification = banned. Claude audits Claude.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L72-73 is the closest line: 'Give it the read the first return got: the three lenses, your worries tested against the artefact… The verifier's green is a claim, not proof. Ask the agent to show what the gate checked.' It stays inside on two counts. First, the rule's own carve-out — 'M5/M6 teach Claude-on-Claude verification' — and the correctness audit here is explicitly delegated to the agent ('Ask the agent to show'). Second, the student's read is diagnostic (which failure mode recurs), not line-by-line correctness checking of a diff. L104's 'Read the scrollback or commits from the re-send; check the agent didn't just stall in the first minute' is a liveness check on the run, not a correctness read of its output.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L73 is the rule's (a) face written into the body almost verbatim: 'The verifier's green is a claim, not proof. Ask the agent to show what the gate checked and what sat outside its view before you credit the kit.' — a copyable push-back that refuses to end the beat on the summary and forces verification at the artefact. L43 does the same for the student's own self-report: 'Where it doesn't, the artefact wins: it is first-hand data from the session itself, and the worry is not.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Offered structures need forced-engagement mechanic.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a student adopts an offered default verbatim, so the articulation the beat exists to produce never happens. Partly present here. L33's prompt hands a fixed four-point checklist ('1) tests are added at every level this repo has, 2) the acceptance criteria pass, 3) documentation is updated, 4) security is reviewed'), and L35 then tells the student to make that definition durable — 'putting the definition in ./CLAUDE.md once' — with no adjacent nudge to adapt the four points to their own repo's bar. Severity is low and this is a TODO, not a gate: the four categories are generic hygiene unlikely to be wrong unmodified, agency over WHETHER and WHERE is explicit at L35, and the maintainer note at L124 records the four points as Antti's deliberate basic done-done. The note forbids adding a done-means criterion and a write-to-CLAUDE.md prompt; it does not forbid an adapt-it clause.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Optional one-clause nudge near L35, e.g. 'adjust the points if your repo's bar differs' — worth adding only if a cohort shows verbatim adoption.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-block hedge naming section's own failure mode = cut-signal, not warning.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read in isolation, the file's hedges name authoring risks, not premise risks. L126: '`## Inspect your results` stays prose, no fence (accepted 2026-08-20). Flagged as M5's only loop-closing diagnostic sitting outside a prompt block. It is deliberate.' Premise-test: remove the hedge and the section still stands — it is a real loop-closing beat for the no-M6 variant, and the hedge defends a FORM choice (no fence) against a re-flagging judge, not a shaky claim. Same for L172's mood-drift watch-for, which names a delivery risk with a trainer fix, not an unverified claim held up by a disclaimer. No 'speculation as authority' or 'unverified anecdote as evidence' hedge anywhere in the block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audience tier determines authoring substrate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101's tier is engineer-IC, and the substrate the body reaches for is the multi-layer CLAUDE.md the rule assigns to that tier: L35, 'putting the definition in ./CLAUDE.md once, where every session reads it… ./CLAUDE.local.md first if you want to live with it a week', with the team/personal split taught at L83. Day-1 install test: nothing to install — both files are plain markdown the runtime already reads. No plugin or skill install is asked for in this module's body, so nothing steals the teaching moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification machinery needs smoke-test before trust.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The verifier BUILD lives in the linked exercise, so this module owns the trust half — and it refuses trust without evidence at L73: 'The verifier's green is a claim, not proof. Ask the agent to show what the gate checked and what sat outside its view before you credit the kit.' That is the rule's 'shows what happened' requirement applied at the point of first use. The module never treats built-as-tested: L74, 'What recurs names your next check. Build it, send again.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Removals are strategic — ask before cutting.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule; the file's own record shows removals were maintainer-directed rather than tidiness-driven, and each carries a do-not-restore note: L141 '**Block is four lines, not five** (Antti 2026-08-27, training run)… do not re-add a fifth', L132 '**The trio pre-announcement is cut** — … handed out all three roles before the student had diagnosed anything', L126 'do not add a fence, and do not cut it', L124 'Do not add a done-means criterion'. Nothing in the body reads as a silently dropped section: the two variant blocks (L67-89, L101-120) both close their markers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Load-bearing platform feature = no fallback. Gate or redesign.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi "just do .* instead|if your environment|doesn.t support|as if you" on the body projection → 0 hits. The load-bearing feature is the git worktree plus a fresh session in it (L173, 'M5 forks a worktree at ../<repo>-m5 and the packaged re-send runs in a fresh session there'), and the module gates on it via the exercise rather than offering a same-repo fallback. L9's 'Stopped, finished, ran out of credit, doesn't matter' is closest to a fallback but concerns the ARTEFACT's state, not substituting a feature — the module still requires a real prior run and never ships a synthetic stand-in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points + UX.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) L200-203 name kinds of org context, not vague slots: 'The student's M4 artefact (Phase 1 source material)', 'Rules-file home (Debrief rewrite target) — ./CLAUDE.local.md', 'The repo's test/CI conventions (Phase 3 shell-hook verifier shape integrates here) — the verifier shape matches what teammates already run'. Each has a downstream prompt where absence dilutes: the third feeds the Phase 3 build, and the per-phase table's Phase 3 row (L231) turns on the same choice. (b) UX: the module's one prompt is a single copy (L33), every named path is discoverable, and the two include links (L49, L51) hand off in order — the worktree exists before the re-send needs it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L205-208 carries exactly three, each falsifiable and each artifact-shaped per the M5/M6 arc-mood carve-out: (2) 'Builds a verifier shaped against the dominant failure mode… Falsifiable: a verifier file exists at a stable path; its first 10 lines name the failure mode it targets'; (3) 'Sends the same task twice with packaging as the changed variable… Falsifiable: two distinct agent runs of the same scoped task exist'. Closest to a competency claim is (1), 'Reads an agent's long-running artefact through three named failure-mode lenses' — a read is not an artifact — but its falsifier repairs it: 'a real artefact-read explains what each lens reveals in specific evidence, not a generic summary', which a working engineer can check on Monday.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a phase ships a forcing function with no trainer lookup when the student gets it wrong. Present for one beat. The table at L223-234 covers eight rows (worktree setup, Phase 1 ×2, Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4, Debrief, closing lecture) — but the module's OWN forcing-function prompt, the done-done opener at L33, has no row, and no bullet in the Push-back moves list (L178-185) names it either. A student whose Claude returns a shallow, thinly-evidenced 'yes, done-done' has no beat-specific recovery; the self-report-skepticism lesson arrives a beat later inside the linked exercise. Non-blocking: the general §31 move (L73) is one section away and the trainer can improvise. Separately, the judge-template cross-check on the existing rows: the worktree-setup row's Connections-blocker recovery (L227 — 'repo commits since M4, files modified, scrollback at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/') is a failure the student can catch in the moment, and its tell is owed in body; see the §65 row.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one row/bullet naming the shallow-done-done failure and a trainer push, e.g. 'which point had the thinnest evidence — ask Claude for the exact transcript line.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Deliberate-antipattern prompts = class-judge exempt, flagged-by-design.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This module is the second half of the rule's own named example ('M4 un-packaged baseline → M5 packaged re-run'), and the design is logged rather than left for a judge to re-flag: L23 'You sent off an un-packaged session', L19 '**Re-send** the packaged version of the same task', and the mood target at L172 makes the contrast the teaching mechanism — 'learning through contrast — I can feel what packaging adds now; I couldn't have read it as a lecture', with the drift to avoid named as 'correction-feeling (my un-packaged run was bad and now I'm fixing it)'. The push-back at L179 restates it for the trainer: 'the un-packaged run was supposed to underdeliver. The diagnosis is data, not blame.' The flagged risk IS what the pair demonstrates → accepted-by-design.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module prose carrying a `**Session**` widget or a `{{prompt:}}` fence is an exercise that has not been extracted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '{{prompt:' on the file → 1, at L33, inside module prose. Harm the rule prevents — an unbroken multi-prompt section getting one giant, unlandable deck slide — is ABSENT: '## Say what done-done means' (L27-35) is its own ## heading, i.e. its own slide, carrying one question. The design is argued at length in the maintainer note at L124 ('the student pastes ae101-m5-done-done into that session… That is the trick: the transcript inspects itself before M5 reads it… Question form rather than a file write for that reason'), and the Transitions row at L168 bills it once ('done-done 3 @start'), so no double-billing. What is actually missing is bookkeeping: the note never invokes §52a, and the corpus's accept-note for this tell — earn-the-trust.md L117, 'The same call covers plan-mode-done-right.md and prework.md, which carry the corpus's only other instances' — is now false, since this file carries a fourth. Non-blocking, and NOT an extraction request.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either add one clause to L124 mirroring earn-the-trust.md L117's accepted-by-design phrasing, or correct that file's 'only other instances' count to name this one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose must not supply an answer its prompt asks for — position is not the test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one prompt (L33) asks 'Are we done-done?' per four points, with evidence from the session. The two lines around it were the risk and both stay legal. L31, 'This one runs in the session you sent off. Its answer lands in the transcript you are about to read', names WHERE the output lands — the (c) constraint/destination keep — and says nothing about what the answer will be. L29, 'A done-done definition is a small context trick that buys repeated fast verification: every run, and every check you build, measures against the same line', is the non-obvious value claim the boundary on (d) explicitly licenses declaring up front. L35 sits below the prompt and moves to a different question (where the definition lives), so it recaps no answer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Multi-session (any new mechanic mid-arc) ships as packaging, not new primitive.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Textbook, and deliberately dosed. The multi-session mechanic gets exactly one clause at L45: 'a session you don't babysit can run beside another' — permission, not a taught beat, with no setup exercise, no lane callouts and no teaching prose built on it. The maintainer note at L145-149 records the budget decision: '**Multisession permission carrier (Antti 2026-08-15): M5 alone, one line** at the close of Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks — control → no babysitting → a second session beside this one. M4 declined.' Diagnostic passes: remove the clause and every beat in the module is still teachable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer blocks point, don't restate. Link architecture doc where they touch delivery.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule B is satisfied at the one place the block touches delivery mechanics, L173: 'Delivery architecture: canonical in training-architecture.md §Working directory model / §Session boundaries. Not restated here.' Other pointers rather than paraphrases: L258 'Pre-cohort open items for M5: see pre-cohort-todos.md', L251 hook reference deferred to claude-code-for-engineers.md §34, L143 'Registry: vocabulary.md verifier-shapes row'. Closest to violating is the internal duplication between the Push-back moves bullets (L178-185) and the per-phase table (L223-234), which restate the same eight pushes — but §25 and §47 each independently require their own block, so this is rule-mandated dual residence with no canonical home elsewhere, not the cross-file duplication §64 governs. Logged as a todo: the pair has already begun to rot (L184 'Same close-the-laptop move' vs L233 'Same step-away move'; L185 'If the term comes up' vs L234 'If the term gets used').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module prerequisite rescue: run it late, never fabricate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a student arrives without a usable prior-module artefact and the body gives them nothing, so they either idle or fabricate. Partly present. M5 load-bears on M4's send-off (L23, 'You sent off an un-packaged session. You walk in with the artefact in front of you'), and grade (a) asks for body blockquote callouts at '## Start here' carrying rescue moves plus an accept-loss floor. '## Start here' (L21-25) carries one blockquote and it is the reading-dosage nag, not a rescue; every rescue move sits trainer-only in the maintainer block (L178, L227). M6 carries the mirror callouts for the identical risk (spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L27-29, 'Packaged session thin or missing? You can still rescue it…' plus 'you lose a bit of value but you can still do this module's exercises'). Mitigation that keeps this non-blocking: L9 pre-authorises the commonest state — 'Walk in with your un-packaged session. Stopped, finished, ran out of credit, doesn't matter' — and the gap is already logged at pre-cohort-todos.md:75 as a consistency call. Sharper sub-case: the done-done prompt asks for 'evidence from this session', and the trainer's rescue hands the student a FRESH session (L178), which would be asked for evidence of a run it never saw.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: One body blockquote at '## Start here' mirroring M6's pair — a rescue move plus the accept-loss floor — and one clause telling a rescued student to point the fresh session at the diff/commits instead of asking it for done-done evidence cold.
